I often hear about how terrible Jimmy Carter was but every specific thing I hear about him sounds pretty good.

The gist of what I know is that he wasn't hawkish, started the ball rolling on a lot of economic liberalization/deregulation, pardoned draft dodgers, and had a fairly sensible energy policy.

Why do people dislike him so much?
Young person here: why should I think Jimmy Carter was a bad president?

Well he wasn't bad in the sense of being evil ordoing anything wrong. He just kind of didn't do anything. He got elected while America was still feeling the affects of Watergate and Vietnam. Nixon resigned in '74,nd his VP Gerald Ford bridged the 2 years before Carter. Vietnam ended in '75. The American citizens were kind of against the government at this time, and saw them as out of touch. This was probably the only reason Jimmy Carter got elected, while most politicians seemed authoritarian and out of touch,Jimmy came acrossed as the strict but loving father figure. He was gonna whip Washington back into shape and give the country a big supportive hug at the same time.

The biggest problem was when he came in he wasn't prepared to handle national or international politics, which were vastly different then what he dealt with in Georgia. And to compound the problem, instead of building his cabinet from the best and brightest America had to offer, he brought his cabinet and support team from Georgia. They were equally inept in the ways of big time politics. Congress, who at this time were just starting to splinter into factions and caucuses, had enough trouble working together, let alone dealing with an outsider president who treated them like inferiors. He constantly tried to micromanage every happening in legislative branch and congresses patients wore thin quickly.

Along with a general distrust in government and rising inflation, Carter also inherited an ever growing energy crisis. Since the early70's, OPEC Nations had been consistently jacking up oil prices. Gas prices soared as the buying power of the dollar dwindled, but Carter and his Cabinet were ill equipt to deal with the problem and got little or no support from Congress. Plus in an effort to get Congress in check he deregulated and defunded a large number of governmental agencies, leaving few programs to help the struggling citizens. And he exasperated the problem by going to the media with the message that they had no short term answers and that citizens were basically gonna have to bite the bullet, asking unions and employees to except a wage freeze. All the while gas prices skyrocketed, and with more of workers income going to gas up their cars no money was going towards other things, thus the economy stagnated further. This was punctuated by a gas shortage that had already weary and angry Americans waiting in long lines for hours and hours to gas up their cars.

At this point , it was abundantly clear that Carter had little ability to handle domestic affairs, but we were about to find out he was equally bad on the world stage. In the late seventies, a lot of countries were starting to emerge as major players, many previously second world Nations were starting to catch up with the first world powers. A lot of isolationist states were starting to expand there diplomatic relations and our long time cold war arch rival the USSR was starting to make diplomatic gains globally, especially in Africa. And then Iran happened. The Despot Shah of Iran was ousted, and to the shagrin of the people of Iran, the ever humanitarian minded Carter allowed him to come to America for cancer treatment. The Iranians retaliated by overtaking the embassy and taking 66 Americans hostage. Carter, other then one failed military rescue mission, mostly tried to broker the release of the captors through diplomacy and bargaining. But by this point, coming of a quagmire in Vietnam and basically sitting on the sideline watching while our nemesis, the USSR expand it's influence on the rest of the world, we were viewed as weak and a fading power. Negotiating from a perceived position of weakness combined with Carter's meek and measured disposition, left America ineffectual in gaining the release of the hostages, and they would remain captives through the rest of Carter's time in office.They were subsequently released the day of Reagan's inauguration, jump starting his presidency and further diminishing the perception of Carter's.

So Carter did nothing to repair domestic issues and even less to maintain America's position on the international power rankings, and has very little positives to counter balance these negatives. The only things of note was brokering an exhaustive peace negotiation between Egypt and Israel, and the Panama Canal Treaty that returned the canal back to Panama's control. Pretty underwhelming.

So all in all, most of the problems that occurred during Jimmy Carter's time in the Whitehouse were results of previous president's and world events, it's the lack of ability or action by Carter and his Cabinet to deal with them that leads to him being considered a bad president. ,
